findings.where: RAMA_AGI_MASTER_SPEC.md — SECTION 28's build ledger, and the missing SECTION 132; the text exists only in docs/research/self-upgrade-build.md §6 under a 'PASTE-READY' heading
findings.problem: RAMA_AGI_MASTER_SPEC.md is unchanged by this slice. Its ledger's last row is 146 (Section 126, the already-reviewed Phase 0 commit), rows 147-151 do not exist, and the spec contains zero occurrences of 'autonomyStop' or 'autonomy.allow' — so four new modules that govern Rāma's autonomy, two new suites and +431 assertions have no entry in the ledger and no recorded next step. The workspace resume protocol exists so a cold session can resume from the document alone; that session would find none of this. The spec is NOT in loyaltyGuard.PROTECTED_FILES, and the immediately preceding commit in this same series (d949b18) added its own Section 126 and ledger row 146 to the spec in the same commit as its code, so the house pattern is that the build commit carries them. The build note even numbers the proposed row 152, five past where the ledger actually ends.
findings.fix: Paste the 'SECTION 132 — The stop built before there was anything to stop' block and the ledger row from docs/research/self-upgrade-build.md §6 (lines 328-408) into RAMA_AGI_MASTER_SPEC.md, renumbering the ledger row from 152 to 147 so it follows 146, and commit them with this slice. Keep the row's 'next step' sentence (the five-stage loop, blocked on design-review findings 2 and 5) since that is the half a cold session needs.

findings.where: electron/lib/autonomyPolicy.cjs — PERMANENT and MASTER_ACT are Object.freeze(new Set([...])); scripts/verifyAutonomyStop.cjs line 323 ('the four frozen constants really are frozen') and line 496 ('the MASTER_ACT subset is exactly two — a third member turns this RED')
findings.problem: Object.freeze on a Set freezes properties, not internal slots, so both exported sets are mutable at runtime. Executed against the live module: Object.isFrozen(policy.PERMANENT) returns true, policy.PERMANENT.delete('revert-own-apply') succeeds and drops the size from 7 to 6, and policy.validate({version:1,levels:{'revert-own-apply':'L0'}}).ok then returns TRUE — a class the design says the data file is never read for becomes readable from it. policy.MASTER_ACT.add('propose-source') succeeds too, so the 'a third member turns this RED' row only holds against a source edit. Nothing is exploitable: requireMasterDriven throws fail-closed for the MASTER_ACT pair once they leave PERMANENT, and all seven permanent classes have FLOORS[c] === CEILINGS[c], so min(CEILINGS[c], declared) cannot exceed the floor even with the permanent check bypassed. It is the assertion that overstates its guarantee, not the fence that leaks.
findings.fix: Export frozen arrays (or a has() closure) instead of the live Sets, or build them with a defensive copy at the export boundary. Replace the Object.isFrozen(policy.PERMANENT) clause at line 323 with the membership assertion already present at lines 339-346, and add a row that mutates a copy and proves the exported view is unaffected.

findings.where: scripts/verifyAutonomyStop.cjs lines 503-510 — check('requireMasterDriven refuses outright for a MASTER_ACT class that is not PERMANENT', /PERMANENT\.has\(classId\)/.test(body) && /throw new Error/.test(body))
findings.problem: This row asserts the second half of the MASTER_ACT/PERMANENT fence by matching two regexes over requireMasterDriven's own source text, which passes for any function that merely mentions the identifier. The behaviour is reachable now: because PERMANENT is a mutable Set (finding 2), deleting 'revert-own-apply' from it and calling policy.requireMasterDriven('revert-own-apply','L4') produces the real throw — verified, message '"revert-own-apply" is a MASTER_ACT class but not a PERMANENT one, so the data file could refuse master's own act'. Every other row in this area asserts behaviour; this is the one that does not, and it guards the loud half of the fence that stops the two sets drifting apart.
findings.fix: Replace the regex row with the executed one: delete a MASTER_ACT member from PERMANENT (or point the module at a test double of the set), assert requireMasterDriven throws with that message, and restore it in a finally. If the sets are made genuinely immutable by finding 2's fix, inject the pair instead so the throw can still be exercised.

findings.where: electron/lib/autonomyGate.cjs — normalise() and namesGovernedPath(); consumed by inspectCreate at both origins and by upgradeApplier.applyWith step 3
findings.problem: path.posix.normalize collapses '.', '..' and repeated separators but does not trim a trailing dot or space from a path segment, so two spellings still read as naming nothing governed. Executed end to end: namesGovernedPath('electron/lib/autonomyStop.cjs.') and namesGovernedPath('electron/lib/autonomyStop.cjs ') both return null, inspectCreate returns no refusal at origin 'ipc' for either, and applyWith with action 'create' APPLIES, leaving 'autonomyStop.cjs.' and 'autonomyStop.cjs ' in electron/lib/ beside the real file. The stop's bytes survive — libuv opens these through the NT path form, so they are genuinely distinct files and the real autonomyStop.cjs was byte-identical afterwards, and action 'patch' is refused earlier with 'does not exist, so there is nothing to patch'. So this is not a write to the governed file; it is the fence answering 'names nothing governed' for a governed-adjacent name, on the one platform whose shell and many of whose APIs do collapse trailing dots and spaces.
findings.fix: In normalise(), after the separator swap and before the comparison, trim trailing dots and spaces from each segment (e.g. split on '/', replace(/[. ]+$/,'') per segment, rejoin) ahead of path.posix.normalize. Then add 'a trailing dot' and 'a trailing space' to the variants() generator in scripts/verifyUpgradeApplier.cjs §13, which already covers the other five spellings at every gate and has the ungoverned-path control rows to keep the fix honest.

findings.problem: The one component in this design that writes Rāma's source never consults 'apply-source', the policy class whose entire description is applying a source change; it resolves 'revert-own-apply' instead. Gating on the safety net before writing is defensible and MASTER_DRIVEN_ENTRIES[0].reason gestures at it, but it is not stated as the reason, and the result is that a reader wiring behaviour onto apply-source later would find the applier does not read it. There is no behavioural difference today: both are MASTER_ACT, both are PERMANENT, and both are pinned FLOOR === CEILING === L4, so the two resolve identically and will keep doing so without a source edit.
findings.fix: Require both — policy.requireMasterDriven('apply-source','L4') alongside the revert class — so the class that names the act is the class consulted, and add a suite row asserting an apply is refused if either resolves below L4. If gating on the revert net alone is deliberate, say so in the step-0 comment rather than leaving it to MASTER_DRIVEN_ENTRIES[0].reason.

findings.where: electron/lib/upgradeApplier.cjs — the proposal.meta.autonomy merge in applyWith's step 0, above the schema check, the loyalty guard, the governed-path fence and the per-change validations
findings.problem: meta.autonomy is written with appliedBy: 'master', autonomousApply: false and recordedAt before any entry validation runs, and it mutates the ledger's own entry object. When a validation then throws, proposals.cjs's apply() catch block sets p.status = STATUS.FAILED and calls log('failed', p, ...) on that same mutated object (lines 244-248), so an entry refused at the door persists a record saying master applied it. The status and reason sit beside it so both facts are retrievable, but a field named appliedBy on a FAILED entry is the badge-label mismatch in the audit trail of the one component that writes source.
findings.fix: Either move the merge below the validations, just before the snapshot, or keep it where it is — recording the attempt has value — and rename the pair to attemptedBy / attemptedAt, setting appliedBy only on the success path. Add a suite row asserting a refused apply leaves no field claiming the apply happened.

findings.where: electron/lib/autonomyStop.cjs — the module header's 'isHalted() governs the PRE-EXISTING dispatchers in PRE_EXISTING' and PRE_EXISTING[].governedBy: 'isHalted'; scripts/verifyAutonomyStop.cjs line 250
findings.problem: isHalted() has no production consumer anywhere. Grepped across electron/, src/ and scripts/: every reference is inside autonomyStop.cjs itself or in the two suites. So governedBy: 'isHalted' records an intention rather than a mechanism, and the suite row '<fn> is governed by isHalted(), not by the fail-safe predicate' passes by reading that hardcoded data field — four green rows over a predicate nothing calls, two lines above a row that asserts those same files contain no reference to the stop at all. The slice is right not to tear the timers down and discloses it three other ways (haltedByEngage: false per entry, engage().teardown.performed === false, and statusText() saying 'Still ARMED, because this build does not tear them down'), so nothing user-visible lies; it is the header sentence and the row's label that claim a mechanism that is not there.
findings.fix: Reword the header to 'isHalted() is the predicate these dispatchers WILL consult; nothing calls it yet' and rename the field to governedByWhenBuilt, or have the suite row say it asserts the declaration rather than the behaviour. Keep the four rows — they are the right rows once a consumer exists.

findings.where: electron/lib/upgradeApplier.cjs — the catch around the write loop, revert() and the stop.engage() call inside revert's failure branch; defaultIo's repoRoot = path.resolve(__dirname, '..', '..')
findings.problem: When a write fails because the DESTINATION is unwritable rather than because of anything about the change, revert() restores by writing the snapshotted bytes back to those same unwritable paths, so it fails too; failures is non-empty, fatal.json is written and stop.engage() revokes master's allow-file and records a halt. A read-only checkout, a permissions change, or a packaged install where repoRoot resolves inside app.asar therefore turns a correctly-approved apply into 'FATAL ... and autonomy has been halted'. The fail-safe fires on a mundane environment problem, and the message points at a revert bug rather than at the real cause. Harm is bounded and recoverable by hand — master writes the allow-file by hand anyway, since lift() cannot succeed until system.suspend-autonomy exists — and the build note already lists 'the app has never booted with these modules loaded' and 'app.getPath(userData) was never resolved' as not verified. Traced through the code; not executed against a read-only fixture.
findings.fix: Before taking the snapshot, probe each target for writability (fs.accessSync(dir, fs.constants.W_OK) on the parent, or an open-for-append on an existing file) and throw a plain refusal naming the path and the permission if any fails, so the revert path is never entered for a cause it cannot fix. Add a suite row with an io.fs whose writeFileSync always throws EACCES, asserting the apply is refused cleanly and stop.isHalted() stays false.
